title: Ochre Systems mid-year health & roadmap alignment

Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Avery Park (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (Head of MLOps, Ochre), Evan Brooks (VP Eng, Ochre), Samir Patel (SRE, Ochre), Nadia Ali (Security, Ochre)

transcript:
[00:00] Liam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Marta (Ochre): Marta here.
[00:08] Evan (Ochre): Evan, hi.
[00:10] Samir (Ochre): Samir here.
[00:12] Liam: Great, Priya and Avery from our side as well, thanks. Goal today is a mid-year health check — usage, cost spikes, reliability, and planning for Q3.
[00:28] Priya (Redwood SE): I'll call out the technical bits, esp around the recommender. We saw the May anomalies in your logs, Marta, a sustained tail of long sequences which increased KV cache churn.
[00:42] Marta: Yeah that started after the new personalization rollout — we expected a little more load but not the 2x tail. Some of our batch jobs also hit it, so maybe a misconfigured replayer.
[00:55] Evan: To be clear the user-facing latency didn't go to hell, but cost spiked because of repeated prefix requests.
[01:05] Priya: Exactly, cost vs latency tradeoff. We suggested prefix caching and a slight increase to batching window, but we know you have tight latency SLOs for recommendations.
[01:20] Samir: Can you explain prefix caching again? I think the term you used was KV cache but sometimes I see it as key-value, sometimes as a prefix store, sorry.
[01:30] Priya: Totally — KV cache is the model's key-value cache for attention states, prefix caching means if many requests share an initial conversation or context we can reuse that state rather than re-computing, saves tokens.
[01:45] Marta: Is there any risk to accuracy when we use cached prefixes? Some personalization signals change fast.
[01:52] Priya: Good question. For rapidly changing user context you can shorten cache TTLs or only cache stable prefixes. There's a small chance of stale context but we can instrument a quick validation to detect drift.
[02:07] Liam: From a product POV, we also have options around quantization. For recommendation models we've seen 4-bit INTQ provide big savings but requires evaluation.
[02:20] Evan: Any rough numbers? Like percent cost drop?
[02:24] Priya: Ballpark 30-45% reduction on GPU inference costs for that model family, depends on perf delta. We'll include perf regressions in the benchmark.
[02:35] Nadia (Security): On the security front, we need to see KMS integration docs and proof that logs with PII are not stored outside our tenancy. We're also verifying SOC2 evidence.
[02:48] Avery (CSM): We'll get the SOC2 packet, and Priya will send the KMS/credentials flow.
[02:55] Nadia: Also SAML mapping — roles need to map into your RBAC console or else we can't grant dev vs prod access.
[03:05] Priya: We support SAML/SCIM and can map groups to roles; I'll attach a mapping example.
[03:12] Marta: Back to cost — the weird thing was two short bursts where cost jumped 3x for a 10 minute window. Any way to protect?
[03:22] Priya: We can set burst caps and autoscale ceilings per-route. Also implement a fallback model (cheaper variant) for overload windows. That provides graceful degradation.
[03:33] Evan: Would fallback mean different quality? We worry about user friction.
[03:37] Liam: Typically yes, fallback to a cheaper quantized or smaller model — we can route a small canary percentage to observe UX before full fallback.
[03:47] Samir: For the May incident, do you have logs that show the source? I can share our tracing IDs.
[03:55] Priya: We pulled the trace; looks like a misconfigured replayer hitting synthetic traffic and not honoring our caching hints. If you share the replay config we'll reproduce locally.
[04:07] Marta: We'll share that right after.
[04:11] Liam: On Dedicated pilot — quick feasibility check: you were interested in a reserved pool for recommendations to guarantee throughput?
[04:20] Marta: Yes, we want predictable latency during peak sale windows and data isolation.
[04:26] Priya: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and optionally private networking. There are commit terms; we can propose a short pilot reservation to see benefits.
[04:36] Evan: How long is a pilot? We don't want to lock long-term.
[04:39] Liam: Pilot can be 30 days with a minimal commit, or a short burst reservation. We'll provide a cost comparison.
[04:47] Nadia: For private deployments we need HSM/KMS patterns documented and the audit log retention policy.
[04:54] Priya: We'll provide both KMS and HSM options, and a sample retention config.
[05:00] Marta: Ok, about the benchmark — what are you proposing?
[05:04] Priya: A 72-hour load run against your recommendation endpoint using your traffic profile, with a control group routing to hosted and an experiment routing to Dedicated + quantized model. We'll measure latency P95, error rates, and token-unit cost.
[05:20] Samir: We'll need to sanitize traces; can you run with obfuscated IDs?
[05:25] Priya: Absolutely — privacy-first trace ingestion.
[05:28] Liam: Also want to call out our Optimize recommendations — small batching and TTL adjustments often yield 15-20% savings without model changes.
[05:39] Evan: If you can show that in the cost model it makes it easier to justify.
[05:43] Liam: We'll include a conservative and optimistic scenario in the cost spreadsheet.
[05:48] [10:02] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[10:12] Marta: Quick question about traffic shaping — can Redwood enforce per-user rate limits inside Dedicated?
[10:18] Priya: We can apply per-API-key throttles and route policies; per-user rate limit can be implemented in front of the inference endpoint in your infra or with a token-mapper at edge.
[10:30] Evan: For observability, we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-model dashboards — do you have a demo?
[10:36] Avery: Yes we have dashboards; we'll share dashboard links and a short screencast showing how to slice by route and token.
[10:42] Samir: One more on SSO — our SAML provider requires attribute encryption, will that break provisioning?
[10:50] Priya: We support encrypted assertions; sometimes there's a cert exchange detail but we've done that with Okta and Azure.
[10:58] Nadia: And for compliance, the SOC2 package should include evidence around change logs and access reviews.
[11:05] Avery: We'll pull the change log examples and the annual access review artifact.
[11:12] Liam: Let's talk timeline. We recommend benchmark week beginning 2026-06-23, share configs by 6/18, run 72 hours, meet to review results week of 6/30.
[11:25] Marta: Sounds good. Two asks: please include a cost-sensitivity analysis and a fallback UX plan.
[11:33] Priya: Will do — we'll include fallback latency deltas and a sample canary rollout playbook.
[11:40] Evan: Any dependencies from our side?
[11:43] Liam: Your main dependency is traffic profile and the replayer config, and security contacts for KMS access.
[11:50] Marta: I'll send the replay config today and confirm pilot stakeholders.
[11:55] [20:00] Priya: Noting that our benchmark will also evaluate quantization regression tests — we'll run an eval harness against your golden prompts.
[20:12] Samir: We'll prepare a small golden set, ~500 prompts, with expected labels.
[20:20] Liam: Great. Any final concerns?
[20:24] Nadia: Please redact any PII before storage.
[20:27] Avery: Acknowledged.
[20:30] Liam: Okay final recap — Redwood will share benchmark plan, SOC2/KMS docs, and a cost model. Ochre will share replay config, traffic profile, pilot stakeholders, and golden prompt set. Follow-up call scheduled after benchmark. Thanks everyone.
[20:48] Marta: Thanks all.
[20:50] Evan: Thanks.
[20:52] Samir: Bye.
[20:54] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
notes_on_transcription: Some speaker labels are generic where the recorder misattributed fast cross-talk. A few technical terms were transcribed imperfectly (eg 'kv cache' spelled 'key value cash' in some lines). Overall medium quality: enough to reconstruct action items and technical asks.
meta_comments: This call followed a recent May reliability incident; customer is motivated to run a short Dedicated pilot but is cautious on commit terms. Security/compliance gating is the most likely blocker to pilot start. Prioritize SOC2 artifacts and KMS HSM patterns in the follow-up packet.
